title: Context mesh: resilient request-context federation and TTL propagation
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: We observe sporadic loss or truncation of request context (trace id, request-scoped tags, routing hints) across heterogeneous transports (HTTP/gRPC/ws) when headers exceed size limits or when legacy SDKs strip unknown headers. This causes gaps in traces, mis-attributed latency, and higher error triage time.

Goal: Implement a robust "context mesh" shim in core SDKs and the edge proxy that: (1) federates context pieces across multiple carriers (headers, query, small cookie, binary frames), (2) encodes a compact TTL-forwarded context stamp so downstream services can recover context even on partial carrier loss, and (3) provides a graceful fallback strategy when headers are truncated — preferring deterministic parent selection and best-effort stitching.

Scope: SDK middleware changes (JS/Go/Python), edge proxy header muxing, short-lived context TTL stamp format, guidelines for service-side reconcilers, and telemetry to measure context-loss rate. Not in scope: full redesign of all third-party clients.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDK middleware added to JS/Go/Python that creates/consumes TTL context stamp and tries alternative carriers when headers missing; 2) Edge proxy can read and write the TTL stamp and performs header muxing without increasing p95 latency by >1ms on standard workloads; 3) Automated tests demonstrate cross-protocol stitch (HTTP -> gRPC -> ws) preserving trace id in 10/10 synthetic scenarios; 4) New dashboard tile shows context-loss-rate < 0.05% for canary traffic and rollback policy if >0.2%; 5) Backwards-compat shim: when legacy clients omit stamp, services still accept upstream trace via existing trace headers.
tasks: Design compact TTL stamp wire format (8-12 bytes encoded) and backwards compatibility mode
Implement JS SDK middleware: stamp emit/consume + carrier fallbacks
Implement Go SDK middleware and server filter for gRPC interceptors
Edge proxy: header multiplexer + stamp inserter, ensure header size guardrails
Add unit/integration tests for truncated-header scenarios and carrier fallbacks
Create canary rollout plan + feature flag in Console
Add observability: metric for context-stamp-missing, context-stamp-recovered, and stitch-failures
Update docs and SDK migration guide
notes: We intentionally target a tiny TTL stamp to avoid busting existing header size limits; design doc explores 2 formats: base64(8 bytes) vs compact varint sequence.
Perf budget: middleware MUST add <1% p95 overhead and <0.5ms median; edge proxy change must be micro-optimized and benchmarked.
Security: stamp must not contain PII; only opaque identifiers and low-entropy routing hints. KMS not required for stamp but edge will sign stamp optionally in enterprise builds (follow-up ticket).
risks: Header bloat leading to downstream 431 errors — mitigated by strict size checks and optional cookie/binary carriers
Inconsistent carrier support in older proxies causing partial recovery — mitigation: feature flag and canary on controlled regions
Cross-language encode/decode mismatch — mitigation: golden-format test vectors and CI contract tests for each SDK
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Merge SDK middleware behind feature flag; unit and contract tests; deploy to staging
Phase 2: Canary ~5% traffic in us-east; measure context-loss and latency; keep flag off for external customers
Phase 3: Enable edge proxy mux on dedicated infra; monitor for 48h; if context-loss <= 0.05% and latency within budget, ramp to 50%
Phase 4: Document and flip default for new SDK versions; provide migration guide for older clients
testing_plan: Synthetic cross-protocol trace rehearse (HTTP->gRPC->ws) with deliberate header truncation
Fuzz test stamp parsing with malformed/old-stamp variants
Load test edge proxy with header muxing at peak QPS and measure p95/p99 impact
Contract CI: add golden vector checks for encoder/decoder across SDKs
